headline: Kansas governor: a winner mark that appeared, then did not
what_happened: The night poller logged a new call for Holscher from CNN's AP feed at the 2026-11-08T20:58 ET read, 99 percent of the expected vote in, margin 0.7 points toward the Democrat (retrieved, data/dashboard/night_poller.log). At the 2026-11-09T07:53 ET read the feed carried no winner, and the board returned the race to pending with the note that a call was logged then withdrawn (retrieved, data/resolutions.json). A live read of the same feed at about 11:30 ET on Nov 9 still shows no winner: Holscher 551,250, Masterson 543,612, 99 percent reporting (retrieved). The night board estimates about 11,000 ballots outstanding on AP's expected vote and says Masterson would need 84.5 percent of them (inferred, data/dashboard/night.json). The Kansas Secretary of State results site returns HTTP 403 to scripts, so there is no official read (retrieved). Whether AP retracted a formal call or the feed's winner field flickered is not known from our data (inferred). Our number is 53.56 for Holscher with a margin of +0.4 (core model). The run had 30 and the lock 27. Polymarket and Kalshi price Holscher at 99.6 (retrieved, 11:24 ET).
why_it_moved: A data-feed event, not a count event. The vote totals are the same before and after the mark came and went (retrieved). The lead of 7,638 votes against roughly 11,000 outstanding is why the markets sit at 99.6 and why the night board scored it as called for a morning (inferred).
should_it_move_us: No. The item grades on the certified result, and the count did not move. The model's number stands at 53.56 until the grade, and the markets already treat it as decided.
trigger: A call that stays in the feed, or the county canvass totals. The one fact that matters is how many ballots are actually left, provisional ballots included, against the 7,638 vote lead.
